No husky, lefthook or pre-commit framework; only tools/pre-commit and tools/commit-msg, both warn-only
No i18n-tasks, syncpack, manypkg, sherif or yarn constraints
No locale key-parity gate: the source catalog (locale/en) is generated by makemessages and gitignored, and translations come from Weblate
No ICU or plural-form checks beyond msgfmt --check-format
Only one pnpm workspace member (starlight_help) and no catalogs, so no cross-manifest dependency-version policy
No per-file license headers; licensing is the single DEP-5 docs/THIRDPARTY file
No CI outside GitHub Actions (no Buildkite, CircleCI, Azure Pipelines, GitLab CI or Jenkins)
No commit-signing or DCO gate; gitlint is skipped in CI as flaky
unusual: About 100 hand-written zulint regex rules (tools/linter_lib/custom_check.py) make up most of the addressable surface. They are meta-tested by tools/tests/test_zulint_custom_rules.py:23-66: bad_lines must match, good_lines must not, exclude and exclude_line paths must exist, and extensionless include_only entries must end with '/'. The linter configuration has its own tests.

zulint is a git dependency (pyproject.toml:373, uv.lock:7069-7071) and is not in the clone, so its matching model had to be inferred from CI passing. Each pattern runs over the whole file, with \A as the file start. Symlinks are dropped, and any path containing custom_check.py is skipped.

Agent-facing rules duplicate contributor conventions: AGENTS.md, .claude/rules/api-changelog.md and .claude/skills (with evals). For example, the ban on a **Feature level** heading in unmerged changelog fragments is stated in .claude/rules/api-changelog.md:17.

The API feature-level workflow uses ZF-<hex> placeholder fragments in api_docs/unmerged.d. tools/merge-api-changelogs merges them. A separate workflow fails if a ZF- placeholder survives (api-docs-update-check.yml), and another fails if the API changed without a changelog entry.
Translations come from Weblate. Unicode NFC normalization of locale files is enforced only by the maintainer script tools/i18n/sync-translations:49-60, not in CI.

docs/THIRDPARTY is a DEP-5 file validated by python-debian: format header, Files globs against git ls-files, license text presence, and a byte-for-byte canonical dump round-trip. The checker injects a fake path so the generated emoji tree resolves (tools/check-thirdparty:45-47).
A Puppet layering firewall (only profiles may include zulip::profile, kandra::profile or the base classes) is enforced by regex rather than by a Puppet tool.
check-executables reads file modes from git ls-tree rather than the filesystem (tools/ci/check-executables:3).
The supply-chain release-age policy is set on both resolvers: pnpm minimumReleaseAge 1440 and uv exclude-newer "24 hours".
gitlint is configured with a custom imperative-mood rule but is skipped in CI as "flaky" (zulip-ci.yml:152,188). Both local hooks swallow failures, so commit discipline rests on docs and review.
About 45 keep-in-sync comments. Three tie literal values (tusd pin, Cloud price, dropdown height) and are expressible as cross_file. The rest tie code or prose behavior.
.sonarcloud.properties is present, but SonarCloud is an external app, not a CI gate in the repository.
check_result:
Final state: validate-config reports "Config valid: 171 rule(s) loaded". 147 rules are defined in the file and the rest come from the extended toolchain-pins@v1 bundle, which is inert. `alint -c CONFIG check . --compact` on the clone prints "all rules passed." and exits 0. Afterwards git status on the clone is empty and HEAD is still 39bd5f2f40a647af06b1cc0267cddd34f88ed2e9.

Violations seen during iteration, and how each was resolved:

(1) zulip-thirdparty-files-token1 flagged static/generated/emoji/images/emoji/unicode/*. That tree is generated, and check-thirdparty injects a fake path so the glob resolves. Excluded with a no-lookahead "not static/generated/" prefix regex.

(2) zulip-yaml-parses reported an analysis failure on the multi-document pnpm-lock.yaml. check-openapi.ts returns early when a file has more than one document, so the file was excluded.

(3) The first custom_check run gave 24 errors:
- 19 were in tools/linter_lib/custom_check.py itself. zulint skips any path containing "custom_check.py", so that path is now excluded from every custom_check rule.
- 4 were shebang-rule hits on #! lines inside Python strings (zerver/openapi/markdown_extension.py:69 and :79, tools/droplets/create.py:138 and :160). CI passes on these, so zulint's \A must mean the file start. The shebang rules were rewritten as start-of-file patterns.
- 1 was zulip-cc-docs-relative-links on docs/contributing/reporting-security-vulnerabilities.md, a symlink to SECURITY.md. zulint drops symlinks.

(4) A global `ignore:` of the 13 tracked symlinks broke zulip-thirdparty-files-token1 (docs/code-of-conduct.md) and zulip-custom-check-paths-exist, because those rules must see symlinked paths. It was replaced with per-rule excludes of the 8 symlinked .md/.json files on the 20 custom_check rules that select those types. scripts/start-server was removed from the extensionless-python list.

Each fix reflects the repository's own gate semantics. No real violation was suppressed.

Non-vacuity was also checked in scratch. All 115 custom_check rules, including the 9 exempt companions, fired on a scratch tree of known-bad lines (mostly custom_check.py's own bad_lines). The exempt companions passed their allowed lines and fired on other lines in the same files.

R4 was confirmed in both directions for all locale and dep-version A units, for the C unit zulip-07, and for the five value-add rules.
stage_b_config_issues: Value-add mislabelled: zulip-va-feature-level-sync is enforced by tools/release:96-100 (grep -F -x '**Feature level N**' api_docs/changelog.md), so it belongs in the ratio (zulip-b06). The enforced relation is membership (cross_file subset), not equality with the first heading, and it should be level: error.

zulip-04 (zulip-locale-translations-json-parses) does not express its unit. compilemessages.py:147-160 calls orjson.loads(...).values(), which needs a top-level JSON object. On a scratch copy, a top-level array ["a","b"] in de/translations.json PASSES the rule. Add an object-root assertion (for example a json_path type or shape check) alongside the parse check. Truncated JSON does fire (resource_parse analysis failure, rc=1).

zulip-28 does not express the duplicate-key part of its unit. tools/check-openapi.ts parses with the yaml Composer, whose doc.errors include duplicate keys (uniqueKeys defaults to true). alint's YAML parse accepted a scratch file with a duplicate mapping key, while correctly rejecting syntax errors and multi-document files.

zulip-21: the fold direction is mismatched. tools/lint runs `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 sort -cf`, which folds to UPPERCASE, while alint lexical-ci folds to lowercase. On scratch input, lines 'aax' then 'a_x' fire in alint but pass sort -cf, and the reverse order passes alint but fails sort. The two disagree for '[', '\\', ']', '^', '_' and '`' against letters. The rule passes at the pin, but it is not the same assertion.

zulip-39 (EXEMPT_FILES entries exist) checks only existence. tools/test-js-with-node:511 computes EXEMPT_FILES - all_js_files, where all_js_files is the non-recursive globs web/src/*.js|*.ts, web/src/billing/*.js, web/tests/*.cjs and web/tests/lib/*.cjs. An exempt entry that exists outside those globs (for example a nested web/src/a/b.ts) would fail CI but pass the rule. The scope should be narrowed to those globs.

zulip-49 over-collapses. At least two of its 'keep in sync' pairs are literal values, not code or prose: MAX_IDX (validator.py:481-482 against poll_data.ts:78 and todo_data.ts:9) and the upload resize dimensions (thumbnail.py:20-29,213-214,233-234 against upload_widget.ts:209-226). They are A (zulip-b03, zulip-b04), and the header's 'three keep in sync value conventions' undercounts. The remaining items checked (500.html/5xx.html prose, zulip_tools.py:68 against provision_inner.py:390, the message_edit buffers, realms.py '600') are correctly D or stale.

zulip-02 wording: the .po files carry both python-brace-format and python-format flags (locale/de: 306 python-brace-format, 183 python-format), and msgfmt --check-format checks both. The summary 'python-format entries' understates the placeholder families a future extractor must handle.

zulip-26 (no ZF- placeholder) is a property of main only. check-feature-level-updated runs on push to main (api-docs-update-check.yml:3-7), and in-flight PR branches legitimately carry ZF-xxxxxx placeholders until merge. The rule is correct at the pin, but adopted as a PR gate it would false-positive. Note it in the rule comment.

I checked absent_categories: 'No ICU or plural-form checks beyond msgfmt --check-format' is CORRECT. GNU msgfmt (gettext-tools 1.0) run on hand-written scratch .po files with --check-format alone exits 0 on both too few and too many msgstr[n] for nplurals=2. Only -c (header checks) reports the 'nplurals = 2... but some messages have only one plural form' error, and Django compilemessages passes only --check-format. So no plural-count unit is enforced.

Reproduced: validate-config gives '171 rule(s) loaded', and check against the clone passes (rc=0). The locale and dep-version A fire tests were reproduced on scratch copies. zulip-03 fires when fr/translations.json is removed. zulip-04 fires on truncated JSON (see the array gap above). zulip-07 fires when the Language-Team line is dropped. zulip-13 fires on tusd version 2.9.2, an altered install-tusd amd64 sha, an altered common.pp tusd aarch64 sha, and a deleted tusd amd64 line, and correctly does NOT fire when the unrelated golang aarch64 sha changes. There are no toolchain-pin A units; the bundled toolchain-pins@v1 extend is inert, as Stage A states.
stage_b_summary:
Stage B for zulip/zulip at 39bd5f2f40a647af06b1cc0267cddd34f88ed2e9.

Stage A's config is valid (171 rules) and passes on the clone. Every locale and dep-version A fire test reproduces (zulip-03, -04, -07, -13). Stage A's custom_check enumeration matches custom_check.py, and the clone stayed clean at the pin.

**Missed units: 9 (6 net in the ratio)**
- Five A units:
  - b01: no BOM in django.po (locale, no_bom). Enforced by Django compilemessages has_bom, and msgfmt also rejects a BOM.
  - b03: MAX_IDX server/client sync.
  - b04: upload resize dimensions equal the thumbnail.py constants (4 cross_file rules).
  - b05: every release-tarball-exclude.txt entry exists (registry_paths_resolve). build-release-tarball's rm -r under set -eu enforces it in production-suite.
  - b06: API_FEATURE_LEVEL is documented in the API changelog, enforced by tools/release:96-100. It promotes Stage A's value-add feature-level rule.
  - All five pass on the clone and fired on broken scratch copies.
- Four D units:
  - b07: the release-time version, date and commit checks.
  - b08: coverage-converse lists.
  - b09: every template rendered by a test.
  - b10: sha256/version verification of the lint tool downloads.
- I dropped a candidate plural-count unit after probing msgfmt. --check-format alone does not check nplurals; only -c does, and Django passes only --check-format. So Stage A's absent-category claim is correct.

**Reclassifications: 9**
- Six D to C: zulip-55, -56, -57, -59, -60 and -15.
  - git_commit_subject_matches, git_commit_message and pair_changed_together express them. The v0.12 corpus counted the same shape as A (pnpm). They are barred only by section 2.4's depth-1 git-kind rule.
  - zulip-60 may be a notifier guard rather than a gate.
- Three family changes, locale to other: zulip-06, -08 and -09. They are source-string checks, consistent with how Stage A tags the cc i18n-markup rules.

**Removal: 1**
- zulip-85: the tarball's zerver/tests grep can never match because of the archive prefix, so the check is dead. Its real exclusion is now b05.

**Config issues**
- zulip-04 accepts a top-level JSON array, but compilemessages calls .values().
- zulip-28 accepts duplicate YAML keys, which the yaml Composer reports as errors.
- zulip-21's lexical-ci folds to lowercase while sort -f folds to uppercase, so the two disagree on [\]^_` against letters.
- zulip-39 checks existence only, not membership in the non-recursive globs.
- zulip-49 over-collapses two literal value syncs (b03 and b04).

**Net effect**
- +5 A (4 other, 1 locale), +4 D, 6 D to C, and -1 D (the removal).
- Locale-family D falls by 3 through the family moves.
notes:

FLAG FOR THE PARENT: commit-message and diff units are bucketed D (zulip-55 to 59 gitlint; zulip-60 github-changes-contain-file; zulip-15 PROVISION_VERSION bump). The reasons are that commit and diff history is external state on depth-1 clones and section 2.4 bars git-history kinds. git_commit_subject_matches or git_commit_message would express 55, 56, 57 and most of 59, and pair_changed_together would express 60. The v0.12 pnpm config counted conventional commits as A. If the integrator prefers that precedent, re-bucket 55, 56, 57 and 59 (and possibly 60) to A or C. They could not be confirmed against these clones.

ZULINT SEMANTICS ARE INFERRED: zulint is not vendored and there is no network access. The header comment in custom_check.py:3-9 gives the exclude, exclude_line and include_only semantics. The rest was inferred from CI passing on the pinned tree:
- whole-file matching where \A is the file start;
- symlinks dropped;
- custom_check.py self-skip.

Translation approximations:
- include_only substrings become `**/<x>/**` globs.
- exclude prefixes become `<x>/**`.
- exclude_line becomes a companion "-exempt" rule that accepts any listed line in any listed file (a slight relaxation).
- Lookaheads become select+require. Lines with several occurrences can differ, for example the placeholder rule and the type-comment rule.
- Extensionless python-shebang scripts (83 at the pin) are listed explicitly, because alint cannot select files by shebang. New scripts need adding.
- The custom_check rules that ask for translatable source strings (cc-13, 15-19, 33, 35, 56, 59, 61, 62, 66-70) are tagged "other". Section 2.3's locale family covers locale files, not source markup.
- check-frontend-i18n and check-capitalization are tagged locale because they check extracted catalog strings.

OTHER NOTES:
- zulip-02 cites Django's own compilemessages, which passes --check-format to msgfmt. That is from knowledge of the Django source; it is not in the clone.
- zulip-04 fires as a resource_parse analysis failure (exit 1), not as a policy violation.
- zulip-07 is C because the true condition depends on Django's LANG_INFO.
- zulip-27 passes vacuously at the pin (no unmerged.d fragments).
- zulint may also report unmatched exclude_line entries. This could not be verified offline, so it was not catalogued.
- No spawning, custom-fact or git-history kinds are used.
- The scratch directory <scratch>/zulip-zulip-a has been removed. Only CONFIG remains.

changes.detail: no_bom over locale/*/LC_MESSAGES/django.po, level error, comment cites compilemessages.py:30-31 and provision_inner.py:374-375. Passes on the clone (rc=0). In scratch (de and fr django.po copied), the clean copy passes; prefixing de with EF BB BF fires (rc=1), and so does prefixing it with FF FE (UTF-16LE BOM).

cross_file equals: validator.py (?m)^MAX_IDX = (\d+)$ against poll_data.ts and todo_data.ts (?m)^const MAX_IDX = (\d+);$. Passes on the clone. In scratch the clean copy passes. It fires on poll_data MAX_IDX 999 (1 finding) and on validator.py MAX_IDX 2000 (2 findings, one per target). Renaming todo_data's const also fires: 'no literal value to compare (the target query matched nothing)'.

Four cross_file equals rules. Sources are thumbnail.py MEDIUM_AVATAR_SIZE, DEFAULT_AVATAR_SIZE, MAX_REALM_LOGO_WIDTH and MAX_REALM_LOGO_HEIGHT. Targets are the user_avatar, realm_icon and else-branch resizing_dimension_opts literals in upload_widget.ts; avatar and icon check both maxHeight and maxWidth, and [^}]*? keeps key order irrelevant. All four pass on the clone and on a clean scratch copy. Scratch fires, each only on the intended rule(s): user_avatar maxHeight 400 fires avatar. user_avatar maxWidth 640 with the keys swapped fires avatar. realm_icon maxWidth 64 fires icon. Logo 120x800 fires the width and height rules. Server DEFAULT_AVATAR_SIZE 128 fires icon (2 findings).

registry_paths_resolve on tools/release-tarball-exclude.txt, base lint_root, extract lines with comment "". The script's `read -r` loop has no comment syntax, so every non-blank line counts. Passes on the clone. Scratch tree: the exclude file plus empty placeholders for its 14 entries, each the same kind (file or dir) as in the clone. That tree passes. It fires on removing zproject/test_settings.py, on removing the templates/corporate dir, and on appending a '# comment' line, which the script would also try to rm. Comment cites build-release-tarball:47-49, the actual loop lines; the record says 46-48.

cross_file relation subset, level error, commented as enforced by tools/release:96-100. It checks version.py (?m)^API_FEATURE_LEVEL = (\d+)$ against api_docs/changelog.md (?m)^\*\*Feature level (\d+)\*\*$, matching grep -F -x. Passes on the clone (516). In scratch the clean copy passes. It passes for API_FEATURE_LEVEL 400, which confirms membership rather than newest-heading equality.
Removed the value-add rule, replaced by zulip-feature-level-documented. The header now says four VALUE-ADD rules and lists the release-tarball and feature-level gates.

Companion to the parse probe: file_content_matches '\A[ \t\r\n]*\{' on locale/*/translations.json, so a document that parses and starts with { has an object root. It uses only clone files; no schema exists in the clone (no tracked JSON contains "type": "object"), and JSONPath cannot tell [] from {} or select a scalar root. Passes on the clone (all 55 files start with {). Scratch results: ["a","b"] fires the new rule while the parse probe still passes, reproducing Stage B. [] with leading whitespace fires, and so does "abc". {} with leading whitespace passes both rules. Truncated JSON passes object-root, but the parse probe fires with a resource_parse analysis failure. The comment also records the JSONC gap I verified (see unit_notes).

Narrowed inside registry_paths_resolve via the extract regex: (?m)^        "((?:web/src/[^/".*][^/"*]*\.(?:js|ts)|web/src/billing/...\.js|web/tests/...\.cjs|web/tests/lib/...\.cjs)|[^"\n]*")"?, . An entry in one of the five non-recursive glob shapes is captured bare and must exist (expect: file). Any other entry is captured with its closing quote, so it can never resolve and is reported. The custom message was dropped so the finding names the entry, e.g. entry "web/src/a/b.ts\"" does not resolve. Passes on the clone. The scratch tree (the script plus 285 empty placeholder files) passes. It fires on 6 cases: nested existing web/src/a/b.ts, existing web/src/foo.tsx, existing web/src/billing/x.ts, existing static/js/x.js, a missing in-glob entry, and a deleted listed file. It passes on an existing in-glob web/tests/lib/zz_helper.cjs. Removing the first, middle and last entries' files gave exactly 3 findings, so all 285 entries are extracted.

Bucket comment changed A to C, explaining that sort -f folds to uppercase and lexical-ci to lowercase, so they disagree for [ \ ] ^ _ ` against letters. Rule unchanged. Passes on the clone and on a scratch copy, and fires when the first two entries are swapped. On the same scratch input, 'aax' then 'a_x' fires alint while GNU `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 sort -cf` exits 0; the reverse order passes alint while sort -cf reports disorder (exit 1).

Bucket comment changed A to B-config unique-key, explaining that the probe catches syntax errors but not duplicate mapping keys, which the yaml Composer reports. Rule unchanged; passes on the clone. Checked on scratch: a duplicate-key YAML passes (rc=0) and an unclosed flow sequence fires a resource_parse analysis failure (rc=1).

Comment now says the rule holds on main only. The workflow runs on push to main (api-docs-update-check.yml:3-7), and PR branches carry ZF- placeholders (docs/documentation/api.md:351-367) until merge-api-changelogs replaces them at merge, so as a PR gate it would false-positive. Rule unchanged.

Nothing in the config modelled or claimed zulip-60. The header's api-docs-update-check line now adds that the check runs on push to main only, and that the notify job's github-changes-contain-file step only decides whether a post-merge notification is sent, gates nothing, and has no rule.
Level changed from warning to info to meet the ground rule (VALUE-ADD at level info), and the section header now says 'Kept at info level'. No other change.

unit_notes.note: Directive 5: lexical-ci folds to lowercase and sort -cf to uppercase. Verified both directions on scratch input against GNU sort. Same verdict at the pin, different assertion. The record JSON still shows A.

Directive 5: assertion family unique-key. alint's YAML parse silently keeps the last duplicate key, which I verified on scratch, while check-openapi.ts's Composer reports duplicates as doc.errors. The rule still covers the syntax-error half. The record JSON still shows A.

Directive 3 was met: the object-root assertion was added from clone files only, as a text rule. It fires on a top-level array, an empty array and a scalar, and passes on the clone. My C suggestion rests only on a separate gap I verified. alint's JSON parse is JSONC-tolerant, so a translations.json with a trailing comma or a // comment passes both rules on scratch (rc=0), while orjson.loads in compilemessages rejects it. No strict-JSON option exists, so the parse half is a relaxation of the enforced check. If the integrator treats that as immaterial, A stands.

Directive 4 was met inside registry_paths_resolve. No option narrows the scope, so the extract regex does it: an out-of-glob entry is captured with its closing quote, so it can never resolve. The finding shows the entry with a trailing quote. It is exact on all tested cases, but it relies on that capture trick. Flagged in case the integrator counts the trick as awkward, which would make the unit C.
